claim: Migraine (interictal, eyes closed): lower posterior alpha power than controls
detail: 50 migraine patients (with or without aura) vs 20 healthy controls and 20 tension-type headache patients; resting eyes-closed EEG with topographic mapping. Only the migraine group showed reduced alpha power at posterior areas. The abstract gives posterior areas, not electrodes, so the listed sites are an approximate posterior mapping. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text. Small study from 1992.

cite.title: Alpha rhythm power and the effect of photic stimulation in migraine with brain mapping.

claim: Migraine without aura (pain-free): alpha up in right posterior sources, down in medial frontal sources
detail: 20 unmedicated migraine-without-aura patients and 20 matched controls, 19-channel eyes-closed EEG with LORETA source analysis. Scalp alpha power was higher in migraine at most sites but significant only at right occipital; source analysis showed increased alpha in right precuneus and posterior middle temporal cortex and decreased alpha in medial frontal cortex. Source-localised (LORETA); mapped to the overlying scalp region, so O2 and Fz are approximate. Theta, delta and beta showed no difference. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text.

cite.authors: Clemens B, Bánk J, Piros P, et al.
cite.title: Three-dimensional localization of abnormal EEG activity in migraine: a low resolution electromagnetic tomography (LORETA) study of migraine patients in the pain-free interval.

claim: Classic migraine: lower peak alpha power in the left occipital region than controls
detail: Topographic mapping in 13 common-migraine, 10 classic-migraine and 11 control participants, eyes closed. Peak alpha power and its reactivity were lower in patients; the only significant difference was classic migraine vs controls at left occipital. Common migraine was not significant. The authors judged the differences minor and not useful for telling migraine from non-migraine. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text.

cite.authors: Neufeld MY, Treves TA, Korczyn AD
cite.title: EEG and topographic frequency analysis in common and classic migraine.

claim: Migraine without aura, inter-ictal and ictal phases: lower resting EEG power than controls
detail: 50 episodic migraine patients (inter-ictal 22, pre-ictal 12, ictal 8, post-ictal 8) and 20 controls, 18-electrode eyes-closed resting EEG. Inter-ictal and ictal patients had lower power than controls; pre- and post-ictal groups did not differ. Band-level results were not separated in the passages checked, so all four bands are recorded as down from the paper's summary of lower EEG power; confirm against the tables. Regional results are not used, so sites are whole-head. Cross-sectional phase comparison; the connectivity result is excluded.

cite.authors: Cao Z, Lin CT, Chuang CH, Lai KL, Yang AC, Fuh JL, Wang SJ
cite.title: Resting-state EEG power and coherence vary between migraine phases.

claim: Migraine (interictal): higher lower-alpha (8-10 Hz) resting power over visual areas than controls
detail: Resting eyes-closed alpha over visual cortex before and after a contrast-discrimination task, migraine vs control groups. Lower alpha band (8-10 Hz) power was higher in migraine; additive internal noise did not differ. The abstract names no electrodes, so O1 and O2 are an assumed visual mapping. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text. Group sizes are not given in the abstract.

cite.authors: O'Hare L, Menchinelli F, Durrant SJ
cite.title: Resting-State Alpha-Band Oscillations in Migraine.

claim: Episodic migraine: relative delta fell and beta rose in the 24 hours before an attack
detail: 24 patients (22 women) recorded resting EEG at home with a wireless device for about 2 weeks, averaging 2 attacks each. Relative delta was lower and relative beta higher in the 24 hours before attack onset than on interictal days; the P300 was also reduced. Within-patient comparison with no control group; the device does not name electrodes, so sites are whole-head. Proof-of-concept study, not a diagnostic test. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text.

claim: Migraine during an attack: higher relative theta and delta, lower relative alpha than controls
detail: Migraineurs (during the ictal phase) and healthy controls, resting qEEG. Relative theta rose and relative alpha fell in the patients; relative delta rose over frontocentral regions, more on the symptomatic side, and correlated with severity in 22 patients. The abstract names regions, not electrodes; the sites are an approximate regional mapping. Taken from the abstract; not checked in the full text. Small single-centre study.
